close_reason: Narrowed to canonical-template-aligned fix: align contacts apply_jmap_patch's non-object-intermediate behavior with mail-server (silent no-op, preserves caller data). The P0 silent-clobber bug is gone; 9 new unit tests cover the fixed paths and adjacent behavior. Broader RFC 8620 §5.3 improvements (invalidPatch returns, array-index support) require canonical-template work on mail-server first and are tracked at bd:JMAP-j6ab. Implementation in commit 7449bc7.
description:
Trigger: ContactCard/copy with a copy-spec patch path that traverses through a non-object intermediate, OR a JSON-Pointer-style array index.

Bad behavior (src/card.rs:292-339):

 1. Non-object intermediate: lines 322-330. If the path is e.g. 'name/full' but card.name is null (or a string), the code does '*next = Value::Object(Map::new());' — it silently CLOBBERS the existing value and continues. RFC 8620 §5.3 says paths whose parent does not yet exist on the patched object MUST be rejected with invalidPatch; this silently succeeds AND destroys data. The same applies if the value at that key is an array or scalar.

 2. Array indices: RFC 6901 / RFC 8620 §5.3 allows numeric segments to index into arrays (e.g. 'emails/0/value' against JSContact card.emails which is a Map<String, EmailAddress> in JMAP — so this happens to be OK for JSContact since arrays are not used in top-level shape — but JSContact does have 'name.components' as an array and the related 'address.components' as an array, plus 'photos' / 'media' arrays). A path like 'name/components/0/value' currently becomes name['components']['0']['value'] (object key '0' on a Map), which silently misses array indexing and produces wrong JSON.

 3. Empty key after split on '/': a literal '//' in a path produces an empty-string segment; the code happily inserts/looks up an empty-string key.

 4. No test coverage. The two existing copy tests use single-segment flat patches ('addressBookIds') so none of #1-#3 is exercised.

Fix path: either replace apply_jmap_patch with the shared jmap-server json_merge_patch (which is the helper used by /set, ensuring consistent semantics between /set update and /copy patch), or add array-indexing + invalidPatch error returns and a notCopied entry on path violation. The current divergence between /copy patch semantics (custom) and /set patch semantics (shared json_merge_patch in jmap-server) is itself a maintainer-burden gotcha.

The sibling-template aspect: this 49-line helper is private to crate-jmap-contacts-server. The mail-server canonical sibling has no equivalent (Email/copy doesn't accept arbitrary path patches; only mailboxIds/keywords/receivedAt overrides). So this code path is unique to contacts-server and warrants extra scrutiny.
title: ContactCard/copy apply_jmap_patch silently destroys non-object intermediate values and lacks array-index support
